claims.text: The reported HfNbTiVAl10 alloy has a hierarchical heterostructure.
The proposed machine-learning model incorporates valence electron concentration as an input parameter.
The proposed machine-learning model incorporates short-range order as an input parameter.
Valence electron concentration is a key parameter for predicting the mechanical properties of HfNbTiVAl10.
Short-range order is a key parameter for predicting the mechanical properties of HfNbTiVAl10.
The model can learn relationships between VEC, SRO, and mechanical properties.
Learning relationships between VEC, SRO, and mechanical properties will improve prediction accuracy.
The proposed model can predict Young's modulus more accurately than established simulations.
The proposed model can predict yield strength more accurately than established simulations.
The proposed model can predict fracture-related behavior more accurately than established simulations.
The proposed model can make the specified mechanical-property predictions more rapidly than established simulations.
Model performance may be limited by training-data quality.
Model performance may be limited by training-data quantity.
Model performance may be limited by the complexity of the relationships among VEC, SRO, and mechanical properties.
The magnitude of the gains in accuracy and efficiency depends on model implementation and training-data quality.
The hypothesis is predeclared as falsified if the model is not significantly more accurate than established simulations for at least 80% of independently tested alloys.
